scope: Proposition 6.6 (Finite propagation) of the manuscript “The low-temperature Sherrington–Kirkpatrick fluctuation scale” (preprints/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026/The-low-temperature-Sherrington-Kirkpatrick-fluctuation-scale-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 217 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e0e2e5e34169e701), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 64. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every sequence of comparison families in Definition 6.1 with data (3)–(5), there are fixed positive constants c < C such that every minimizing quantile at a positive strength 0 < λ ≤ d2 satisfies cu ≤ r(u) ≤ Cu nδ √ nE √ λ ≤ u ≤ 1 ! for all sufficiently large n along that sequence. For ordinary admissible bare endpoints, the entire comparison satisfies 0 ≤ V(λ) − fn(b0, h0) ≤ n20δ E, 0 ≤ λ ≤ d2 . For a fixed strength family only the profile assertion is made; its proof uses error estimates exclusively for admissible child endpoints.
